57:25.ar: لَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رُسُلَنَا بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَأَنزَلۡنَا مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ ٱلنَّاسُ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ وَأَنزَلۡنَا ٱلۡحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأۡسࣱ شَدِيدࣱ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥ وَرُسُلَهُۥ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزࣱ‏
57:25.en: We verily sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and revealed with them the Scripture and the Balance, that mankind may observe right measure; and He revealed iron, wherein is mighty power and (many) uses for mankind, and that Allah may know him who helpeth Him and His messengers, though unseen. Lo! Allah is Strong, Almighty

57:26.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا نُوحࣰ ا وَإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَجَعَلۡنَا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا ٱلنُّبُوَّةَ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبَۖ فَمِنۡهُم مُّهۡتَدࣲۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:26.en: And We verily sent Noah and Abraham and placed the prophethood and the scripture among their seed, and among them there is he who goeth right, but many of them are evil-livers

57:27.ar: ثُمَّ قَفَّيۡنَا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم بِرُسُلِنَا وَقَفَّيۡنَا بِعِيسَى ٱبۡنِ مَرۡيَمَ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ٱلۡإِنجِيلَۖ وَجَعَلۡنَا فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ رَأۡفَةࣰ وَرَحۡمَةࣰۚ وَرَهۡبَانِيَّةً ٱبۡتَدَعُوهَا مَا كَتَبۡنَٰهَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ إِلَّا ٱبۡتِغَآءَ رِضۡوَٰنِ ٱللَّهِ فَمَا رَعَوۡهَا حَقَّ رِعَايَتِهَاۖ فَـَٔاتَيۡنَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ أَجۡرَهُمۡۖ وَكَثِيرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ
57:27.en: Then We caused Our messengers to follow in their footsteps; and We caused Jesus, son of Mary, to follow, and gave him the Gospel, and placed compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him. But monasticism they invented - We ordained it not for them - only seeking Allah's pleasure, and they observed it not with right observance. So We give those of them who believe their reward, but many of them are evil-livers

57:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَءَامِنُواْ بِرَسُولِهِۦ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ كِفۡلَيۡنِ مِن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ وَيَجۡعَل لَّكُمۡ نُورࣰ ا تَمۡشُونَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرۡ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
57:28.en: O ye who believe! Be mindful of your duty to Allah and put faith in His messenger. He will give you twofold of His mercy and will appoint for you a light wherein ye shall walk, and will forgive you. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

57:29.ar: لِّئَلَّا يَعۡلَمَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَلَّا يَقۡدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءࣲ مِّن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَأَنَّ ٱلۡفَضۡلَ بِيَدِ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
57:29.en: That the People of the Scripture may know that they control naught of the bounty of Allah, but that the bounty is in Allah's hand to give to whom He will. And Allah is of Infinite Bounty

7:85.ar: وَإِلَىٰ مَدۡيَنَ أَخَاهُمۡ شُعَيۡبࣰ اۚ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ ٱعۡبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنۡ إِلَٰهٍ غَيۡرُهُۥۖ قَدۡ جَآءَتۡكُم بَيِّنَةࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۖ فَأَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ وَلَا تَبۡخَسُواْ ٱلنَّاسَ أَشۡيَآءَهُمۡ وَلَا تُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ بَعۡدَ إِصۡلَٰحِهَاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
7:85.en: And unto Midian (We sent) their brother, Shu'eyb. He said: O my people! Serve Allah. Ye have no other Allah save Him. Lo! a clear proof hath come unto you from your Lord; so give full measure and full weight and wrong not mankind in their goods, and work not confusion in the earth after the fair ordering thereof. That will be better for you, if ye are believers

42:17.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَۗ وَمَا يُدۡرِيكَ لَعَلَّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَرِيبࣱ‏
42:17.en: Allah it is Who hath revealed the Scripture with truth, and the Balance. How canst thou know? It may be that the Hour is nigh

55:7.en: And the sky He hath uplifted; and He hath set the measure

55:8.en: That ye exceed not the measure

55:9.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلۡوَزۡنَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ وَلَا تُخۡسِرُواْ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ
55:9.en: But observe the measure strictly, nor fall short thereof

46:9.ar: قُلۡ مَا كُنتُ بِدۡعࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدۡرِي مَا يُفۡعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمۡۖ إِنۡ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
46:9.en: Say: I am no new thing among the messengers (of Allah), nor know I what will be done with me or with you. I do but follow that which is inspired in me, and I am but a plain warner

19:26.ar: فَكُلِي وَٱشۡرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيۡنࣰ اۖ فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡبَشَرِ أَحَدࣰ ا فَقُولِيٓ إِنِّي نَذَرۡتُ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ صَوۡمࣰ ا فَلَنۡ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ إِنسِيࣰّ ا
19:26.en: So eat and drink and be consoled. And if thou meetest any mortal, say: Lo! I have vowed a fast unto the Beneficent, and may not speak this day to any mortal

8iYLyUjzdfs.speaker: adnan
8iYLyUjzdfs.speaker_note: his own concluding session of the Sunday tafseer of Surat al-Hadid
8iYLyUjzdfs.title: Tafseer of Surat al-Hadid, Part 8: Verses 25-29
8iYLyUjzdfs.one_line: The balance and iron, honest self-criticism of the ummah, monasticism as invented worship that breaks the balance, and the double share of mercy.
8iYLyUjzdfs.summary: He returns to verse 25: the rare word mizan signals that the revealed law is balanced so people can live in prosperous justice, and pairing it with iron, the surah's name, shows the deen needs sincere hearts and people willing to build and defend. He contrasts Western Muslims, who grasp this better, with polarized movements elsewhere, and insists on honest self-criticism of the ummah, since flattering ourselves leads into a wall. Verses 26 and 27 trace prophets following one another with the same balance, then turn to Jesus, whose followers were given compassion but invented monasticism, a celibacy Allah never prescribed and they could not sustain. From this he draws the Quranic meaning of bid'ah: inventing worship Allah did not ask for that cripples a person's functioning. He supports it with the man who vowed to stand in the sun, the young men who vowed never to sleep, break fast or marry, and Abdullah ibn Amr regretting his self-imposed burdens. Good intentions do not redeem bad decisions. He distinguishes such inventions from training exercises for self-knowledge and from beneficial new practices with a sound basis, using a story of a dream declaring Eid. Verses 28 and 29 promise believers a double share of mercy, a light to walk by and forgiveness, and affirm that bounty is in Allah's hand alone.

outline.heading: Opening
The rare word mizan
outline.gist: Apart from Shu'ayb's literal scales, the Balance appears only a few times, each pointing to a faith system that needs proper reference and balanced governance.

outline.heading: Balance for justice, and iron
outline.gist: Righteousness is abstract until practised; the balanced law aims at qist, while iron brings both bloodshed and benefit and tests who supports Allah unseen.

outline.heading: Sincere intentions plus iron
outline.gist: History forgets conquerors who came only for wealth, and ideologies with no one to build or defend them vanish; Islam needs both.

outline.heading: West versus Middle East on this balance
outline.gist: Western Muslims grasp the balance better; elsewhere he saw unorganized spiritual movements on one side and spiritless mechanical ones on the other.

outline.heading: The duty of honest self-criticism
outline.gist: He criticizes the ummah as an insider; self-praise is easy and popular, but we are heading into a brick wall unless we admit it, as the Prophet held himself and those close to him to the highest standard.

outline.heading: Read the Quran projecting it onto yourself
outline.gist: Ask whether your heart and your hands are both engaged; change needs sacrifice, grit and looking in the mirror individually and collectively.

outline.heading: Nuh, Ibrahim and descendants who broke off
outline.gist: Prophethood and scripture stayed in their line; some followed and many 'broke loose' like a blossom from its seed, going in another direction.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recitation notes: pause marks and the connecting hamzah
outline.gist: Pause symbols are scholars' choices that differ between printings, not part of the revealed text; the connecting hamzah is dropped in continuous recitation.

outline.heading: Messengers in each other's footsteps
outline.gist: Qaffayna means sending one directly behind another; laws differed but every prophet brought the same creed and balance, none pure spirituality.

outline.heading: Jesus and the compassion of his followers
outline.gist: He was given the Gospel and his followers' hearts were filled with tenderness and mercy.

outline.heading: Monasticism they invented
outline.gist: Rahbaniyyah, a vow of celibacy and total devotion, was made up without a source; this is the only place the Quran uses the verb of innovation for such a practice.

outline.heading: 'We did not prescribe it' and they did not keep it
outline.gist: Two main readings: Allah only prescribed what pleases Him, or they did it seeking His pleasure; either way they could not observe it as it deserved.

outline.heading: Worship Him only as He asked
outline.gist: We are not asked to go beyond what He explained; everything that pleases Him has already been made clear.

outline.heading: The man who vowed to stand in the sun
outline.gist: The Prophet told him to sit and get out of the sun but complete his fast, since Allah has no need for self-torture.

outline.heading: The young men who vowed to outdo the Prophet
outline.gist: One would fast forever, one pray all night, one never marry; the Prophet said he fears Allah most yet fasts and breaks fast, prays and sleeps, and marries.

outline.heading: Bid'ah in its Quranic sense
outline.gist: Inventing forms of worship Allah did not ask for that remove the material side and cripple functioning; scholars give dozens of definitions, but this is the Quran's example.

outline.heading: Learning without attacking other faiths
outline.gist: He does not occupy himself with demeaning other religions, but this example is one the Quran presents for our learning.

outline.heading: Good intentions don't make up for bad decisions
outline.gist: Celibacy was meant to please God but broke the balance and discredited the Church from within, pushing many away from religion altogether, which Muslims should not celebrate.

outline.heading: The vow of silence
outline.gist: A vow of silence was acceptable in Maryam's law but not in ours; Islam teaches speaking well or holding the tongue, not silence as worship.

outline.heading: Invented worship versus training exercises
outline.gist: Practices from the scholars of tazkiyah are exercises for self-knowledge and growth, not acts of worship, and both their fans and critics often miss the difference.

outline.heading: Testing a practice: recitation before Jumuah
outline.gist: 'The Prophet didn't do it' is not enough; ask whether it was forbidden, whether it lacks any basis, and whether it is claimed as sunnah. Public recitation and teaching have clear foundations.

outline.heading: Why the word bid'ah must be used carefully
outline.gist: A group choosing one night a week for qiyam is not innovating; the word is serious because every innovation leads to misguidance.

outline.heading: Real innovation: revelation after the Prophet
outline.gist: Claiming someone after the Prophet receives revelation or is infallible brings prophethood back into Islam, which ended when Jibril stopped coming.

outline.heading: The dream that declared Eid
outline.gist: A respected villager dreamt the Prophet declared Eid; the mufti answered that the Prophet told him while awake to follow the moon sighting, so the waking law outranks a sincere dream.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Amr's regret
outline.gist: He bargained the Prophet up to finishing the Quran every three days and fasting alternate days, and in old age wished he had accepted the lighter offer; spiritual growth is not self-torment.

outline.heading: They overranked the spirit
outline.gist: Monasticism inflated the spiritual and discarded the physical, and that has never worked.

outline.heading: His week of olives and za'tar
outline.gist: At 18 he spent a week in a cabin eating only olives and za'tar, an exercise that taught him more about self-control and his limits than almost anything, not an act of worship.

outline.heading: We are pampered: care for both equally
outline.gist: The companions were hungry by circumstance; we are so comfortable we need such tests. Care for the heart as much as for the car, the house and a spouse's looks.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recap of the cluster and the closing call
outline.gist: After a cluster of choices, the surah ends by calling believers to mindfulness of Allah and to follow His Messenger.

outline.heading: A double share of mercy
outline.gist: Two shares because the cluster kept offering two options, and al-Hadid asks us to balance two things that seem opposite.

outline.heading: A light to walk by
outline.gist: This recalls the believers' light in verses 12-13: an inner, spiritual light in this world that becomes physical light on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: And He will forgive you
outline.gist: We will not choose rightly every time; there will be aimless years and mechanical prayers, and Allah promises forgiveness for those shortcomings.

outline.heading: So the People of the Book may know
outline.gist: The negation is emphatic in Arabic; those who added to a complete faith must know they have no control over Allah's bounty or how He is worshipped.

outline.heading: All bounty is in Allah's hand
outline.gist: If you want His bounty, listen, keep the balance and follow the path He explained.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Self-criticism of the ummah

themes.label: Prophets in each other's footsteps

themes.label: Training exercises for the self

themes.label: How to judge a new practice

3:96.ar: إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيۡتࣲ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكࣰ ا وَهُدࣰ ى لِّلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
3:96.en: Lo! the first Sanctuary appointed for mankind was that at Becca, a blessed place, a guidance to the peoples

3:97.ar: فِيهِ ءَايَٰتُۢ بَيِّنَٰتࣱ مَّقَامُ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۖ وَمَن دَخَلَهُۥ كَانَ ءَامِنࣰ اۗ وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ حِجُّ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ مَنِ ٱسۡتَطَاعَ إِلَيۡهِ سَبِيلࣰ اۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
3:97.en: Wherein are plain memorials (of Allah's guidance); the place where Abraham stood up to pray; and whosoever entereth it is safe. And pilgrimage to the House is a duty unto Allah for mankind, for him who can find a way thither. As for him who disbelieveth, (let him know that) lo! Allah is Independent of (all) creatures

22:26.ar: وَإِذۡ بَوَّأۡنَا لِإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ مَكَانَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ أَن لَّا تُشۡرِكۡ بِي شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَطَهِّرۡ بَيۡتِيَ لِلطَّآئِفِينَ وَٱلۡقَآئِمِينَ وَٱلرُّكَّعِ ٱلسُّجُودِ
22:26.en: And (remember) when We prepared for Abraham the place of the (holy) House, saying: Ascribe thou no thing as partner unto Me, and purify My House for those who make the round (thereof) and those who stand and those who bow and make prostration

2:127.ar: وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
2:127.en: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, (Abraham prayed): Our Lord! Accept from us (this duty). Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer, the Knower

2:136.ar: قُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ وَٱلۡأَسۡبَاطِ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَمَآ أُوتِيَ ٱلنَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيۡنَ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۡهُمۡ وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ
2:136.en: Say (O Muslims): We believe in Allah and that which is revealed unto us and that which was revealed unto Abraham, and Ishmael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and that which Moses and Jesus received, and that which the prophets received from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and unto Him we have surrendered

7oWiz6LHK2E.speaker_note: speaks as the imam of the masjid and mentions his son; one speaker throughout
7oWiz6LHK2E.title: Hajj, the Uniting Ritual: Followers of the Prophets
7oWiz6LHK2E.one_line: Every prophet made pilgrimage to the first House, so Muslims who follow all the prophets should feel confident, not out of place.
7oWiz6LHK2E.summary: Speaking in the first ten days of Dhul Hijjah, he starts from the verses on the first House of worship at Bakka and notes that khateebs everywhere recite them this week, one of the ways Allah unites the ummah by season. His point is that Hajj was not Ibrahim's or Muhammad's alone: the House predated Ibrahim, who was shown its site to rebuild it, and narrations describe Nuh and many other prophets making the journey, with the Prophet naming valleys and describing earlier prophets passing through in talbiyah. Hajj therefore reminds us of human origins and of a faith that believes in every messenger without distinction. In the second khutbah he draws out the consequence: a Muslim follows every prophet, which should give confidence without arrogance. It is not the woman in hijab, the young man who avoids premarital sex, or the one who prays who owes an explanation; what needs explaining is a way of life no prophet ever taught. It pains him to see youth insecure about their faith. Citing the hadith that Islam began strange and will return strange, he says it is fine to feel a minority as long as one keeps reforming when others lose their moral compass, and asks people to use the ten days to build that confidence.

outline.heading: Opening
The first House at Bakkah
outline.gist: He translates the verses: the first house of worship for people, blessed and a guidance, with clear signs, the station of Ibrahim and safety, and Hajj owed to Allah by those able.

outline.heading: One verse in every masjid: united by season
outline.gist: Khateebs across tens of thousands of masajid recite the same verses this week; Allah gathers the ummah around shared seasons. His thesis: the pilgrimage was made by all prophets, not only Ibrahim and Muhammad.

outline.heading: Ibrahim was shown where the House stood
outline.gist: Allah showed Ibrahim the place of the House, which means it was already there; consistent with the first house being at Makkah, he was shown it so that he could rebuild it.

outline.heading: Every prophet made the pilgrimage
outline.gist: Ibrahim re-raised existing foundations. Scholars narrate that no prophet failed to make Hajj except those occupied with their peoples until death; Nuh came on a camel and found only a small hill of red sand.

outline.heading: The Prophet knew every valley on the road
outline.gist: On the way from Madinah to Makkah he asked the companions the names of each valley and hill; born there, he knew the land road by road.

outline.heading: Earlier prophets passing in talbiyah
outline.gist: At the valley of al-Azraq he described earlier prophets who passed through it on pilgrimage, one in a cloak, raising his voice in talbiyah as he went to Allah.

outline.heading: Seventy prophets at one place
outline.gist: One came on a camel of a known tribal breed, tied it beside the masjid and prayed there; at least seventy prophets passed that spot in talbiyah.

outline.heading: Hajj as a reminder of unity
outline.gist: All prophets who were able made the journey because it is the first House; each season Allah calls all His servants back to the same place.

outline.heading: Back to the origin of the human story
outline.gist: Pilgrims return yearly to where our first parents found and turned around their destiny, to remember who they are and the story they belong to; belief in what was revealed to Ibrahim and all after him is the central message.

outline.heading: No distinction between any of the messengers
outline.gist: Musa, Isa and prophets we do not know were all taught the same thing; whoever does not accept all of them is not Muslim, and Hajj, which they all performed, is a reminder of that.

outline.heading: Interlude
You follow all the prophets: confidence, not vanity
outline.gist: The first House unites us. You are a follower of every prophet without exception; the authenticity of what you belong to should give confidence and comfort, never pride. You did not invent a strange way of life.

outline.heading: Where did you get that from?
outline.gist: Turn the question around: none of the messengers lived the way you are asked to admire. The woman in hijab walks in the footsteps of every pious woman from Adam to Muhammad.

outline.heading: The opposite is what needs explaining
outline.gist: Prayer and chastity need no apology; his son should not have to explain why he avoids premarital sex. The one who lives otherwise must explain where he got it.

outline.heading: Walking where the prophets walked
outline.gist: You have every reason to be confident; Hajj puts you where they stood. Muslims follow all the prophets' teachings, though only the Quran survives authentically.

outline.heading: Youth insecure about their deen
outline.gist: It hurts him to see young Muslims self-conscious, as if they do not belong; the follower of all the messengers does not stand out, others do.

outline.heading: Islam began strange
outline.gist: Muslims never set out to make others feel they do not belong, yet feeling out of place for the prophets' values is bizarre. The hadith in Muslim: Islam began with few followers and will return to that, so feeling out of place is fine.

outline.heading: The strangers reform when others lose their compass
outline.gist: Majority or minority makes no difference if you follow what is right and keep working for reform; use the ten days to build confidence in whose footsteps you walk and the grit to hold on to the end.

outline.heading: Outro

zDzwkpsejgc.title: The Five Categories of Community Investment: Financial Centralization
zDzwkpsejgc.one_line: The fifth category: a population becomes a community only by centralizing something, and Muslims here can realistically centralize their finances.
zDzwkpsejgc.summary: Beginning with the parable of the grain that sprouts seven ears of a hundred grains, he presents the last of his five investment categories, admitting finance is outside his expertise. A group of people, he argues, is only a population until it centralizes something: politics, religious leadership, social life or finances. The first three are not realistic for Canadian Muslims, but finances are. He grounds this in the pledge with the people of Yathrib, whose second condition was committing their wealth, and in the many verses on spending, including the transaction in which Allah buys believers' lives and wealth for Paradise. If this sounds suspicious, he says, it is because trust has eroded, so he stresses the Prophet's transparency: he kept nothing for himself, and rebuked a zakat collector who called his takings gifts. Zakat itself was centrally collected, and Abu Bakr's fight against those who refused to hand it over is why Islam spread at all. In the second khutbah he notes that people trust conventional funds run by those who care nothing for Allah yet scrutinize Islamic endowments. A community fund could stabilize organizations, incentivize practice as the share for those whose hearts are reconciled does, and support marriage, homes, businesses, insurance, schooling and advocacy. He asks those with wealth and financial skill to start working on it.

outline.heading: Opening
The grain that grows seven ears
outline.gist: The believer who spends for Allah is like a single grain producing seven ears of a hundred grains each: Allah multiplies every act of charity many times over.

outline.heading: Start with what we are capable of
outline.gist: The five categories are not sacred, only what the community can actually do; aiming for what is impossible right now keeps people where they are. He left finance for last because it is not his field.

outline.heading: A population becomes a community by centralizing
outline.gist: Without centralizing one of four things, a group with shared beliefs or backgrounds is only a population. Politics cannot be centralized by a religious minority here, though it can advocate.

outline.heading: Only finances can be centralized here
outline.gist: Religious leadership will never be centralized, and social clustering like a Chinatown or Little Italy is not realistic. Finances are the one thing Muslims here can centralize.

outline.heading: The pledge of Yathrib: wealth in ease and hardship
outline.gist: Ideas that change the world always sound insane at first. The second condition the Prophet set for the people of Yathrib was to commit their wealth, a lot or a little, in easy times and hard.

outline.heading: Verse after verse on spending
outline.gist: Their commitment let the Prophet act within his community. He could recite verses on spending wealth for an hour and a half, and recites a string of them.

outline.heading: Strength, and a transaction with Allah
outline.gist: Prepare strength against those hostile to you, which requires wealth; Allah has bought believers' lives and wealth for Paradise. If that sounds suspect, it is because trust has been lost.

outline.heading: The Prophet kept nothing for himself
outline.gist: He gave away even his rightful share before entering his house, so plainly that his wives found the life hard and verses offered them a choice to stay or take a generous divorce.

outline.heading: The collector's 'gift'
outline.gist: A zakat collector set aside a gift he said was his; the Prophet asked whether it would have come had he stayed home, then raised his hands asking Allah to witness. Gifts that come with a public role are a conflict of interest.

outline.heading: Zakat was centralized
outline.gist: The Prophet centralized zakat, and its collectors are one of the eight categories of recipients. Technically it should be gathered and distributed, not given out individually.

outline.heading: Wars over zakat, not apostasy
outline.gist: After the Prophet's death most of the tribes Abu Bakr fought had not abandoned belief; they refused to hand their zakat to the state and wanted to distribute it among themselves.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr's stand is why we are Muslim
outline.gist: He would fight them even over a cord they used to give the Prophet. Scholars agree that keeping zakat centralized let the ummah grow beyond one small region; without centralization we remain a population.

outline.heading: Interlude
Trusting conventional funds, combing through Islamic ones
outline.gist: People put hundreds of thousands into funds run by those who care nothing for Allah, yet scrutinize every detail of an Islamic endowment fund. Regaining trust takes work, but the community and its organizations need stability.

outline.heading: Organizations scrambling for small sums
outline.gist: Islamic organizations argue over programs needing ten or fifteen thousand dollars, which is pathetic for a community that is not poor.

outline.heading: Incentivize being a practising Muslim
outline.gist: Zakat includes a share for those whose hearts are to be reconciled, Muslims distant from practice. People follow the money, so a fund should make belonging pay: help with marriage, homes, businesses and the needy.

outline.heading: Plenty of wealth, not used for ourselves
outline.gist: A fund could replace costly insurance. He knows nothing about money, but the community has a great deal of wealth it does not use for its own interests.

outline.heading: Fund the five categories
outline.gist: A fund could keep schools and education programs running, sustain outreach, and pay lawyers and lobbyists to speak where Muslims are not represented.

outline.heading: Bring even a date
outline.gist: When the Prophet appealed for funds, those with nothing brought a single date and hypocrites laughed. You put in whatever you have, because without centralization there is no strength and no voice.

outline.heading: Those with wealth and skill are obligated
outline.gist: His life is education and mentorship; those blessed with wealth or financial skill must connect and get this done, or the other categories cannot thrive while organizations ask whether they can afford a teacher.

outline.heading: Outro

43:22.ar: بَلۡ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَآ ءَابَآءَنَا عَلَىٰٓ أُمَّةࣲ وَإِنَّا عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِهِم مُّهۡتَدُونَ
43:22.en: Nay, for they say only: Lo! we found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footprints

14:21.ar: وَبَرَزُواْ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَقَالَ ٱلضُّعَفَٰٓؤُاْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمۡ تَبَعࣰ ا فَهَلۡ أَنتُم مُّغۡنُونَ عَنَّا مِنۡ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۚ قَالُواْ لَوۡ هَدَىٰنَا ٱللَّهُ لَهَدَيۡنَٰكُمۡۖ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡنَآ أَجَزِعۡنَآ أَمۡ صَبَرۡنَا مَا لَنَا مِن مَّحِيصࣲ‏
14:21.en: They all come forth unto their Lord. Then those who were despised say unto those who were scornful: We were unto you a following, can ye then avert from us aught of Allah's doom? They say: Had Allah guided us, we should have guided you. Whether we rage or patiently endure is (now) all one for us; we have no place of refuge

71:21.ar: قَالَ نُوحࣱ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمۡ عَصَوۡنِي وَٱتَّبَعُواْ مَن لَّمۡ يَزِدۡهُ مَالُهُۥ وَوَلَدُهُۥٓ إِلَّا خَسَارࣰ ا
71:21.en: Noah said: My Lord! Lo! they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in naught save ruin

71:22.en: And they have plotted a mighty plot

71:23.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَا تَذَرُنَّ ءَالِهَتَكُمۡ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدࣰّ ا وَلَا سُوَاعࣰ ا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسۡرࣰ ا
71:23.en: And they have said: Forsake not your gods. Forsake not Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr

71:24.ar: وَقَدۡ أَضَلُّواْ كَثِيرࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَٰلࣰ ا
71:24.en: And they have led many astray, and Thou increasest the wrong-doers in naught save error

54:10.en: So he cried unto his Lord, saying: I am vanquished, so give help

11:40.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَمۡرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ قُلۡنَا ٱحۡمِلۡ فِيهَا مِن كُلࣲّ زَوۡجَيۡنِ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ وَأَهۡلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَوۡلُ وَمَنۡ ءَامَنَۚ وَمَآ ءَامَنَ مَعَهُۥٓ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣱ‏
11:40.en: (Thus it was) till, when Our commandment came to pass and the oven gushed forth water, We said: Load therein two of every kind, a pair (the male and female), and thy household, save him against whom the word hath gone forth already, and those who believe. And but a few were they who believed with him

11:38.ar: وَيَصۡنَعُ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيۡهِ مَلَأࣱ مِّن قَوۡمِهِۦ سَخِرُواْ مِنۡهُۚ قَالَ إِن تَسۡخَرُواْ مِنَّا فَإِنَّا نَسۡخَرُ مِنكُمۡ كَمَا تَسۡخَرُونَ
11:38.en: And he was building the ship, and every time that chieftains of his people passed him, they made mock of him. He said: Though ye make mock of Us, yet We mock at you even as ye mock

11:45.ar: وَنَادَىٰ نُوحࣱ رَّبَّهُۥ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ ٱبۡنِي مِنۡ أَهۡلِي وَإِنَّ وَعۡدَكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَأَنتَ أَحۡكَمُ ٱلۡحَٰكِمِينَ
11:45.en: And Noah cried unto his Lord and said: My Lord! Lo! my son is of my household! Surely Thy promise is the truth and Thou are the Most Just of Judges

11:46.ar: قَالَ يَٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُۥ لَيۡسَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ عَمَلٌ غَيۡرُ صَٰلِحࣲۖ فَلَا تَسۡـَٔلۡنِ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۖ إِنِّيٓ أَعِظُكَ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
11:46.en: He said: O Noah! Lo! he is not of thy household; lo! he is of evil conduct, so ask not of Me that whereof thou hast no knowledge. I admonish thee lest thou be among the ignorant

11:47.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّيٓ أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنۡ أَسۡـَٔلَكَ مَا لَيۡسَ لِي بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱۖ وَإِلَّا تَغۡفِرۡ لِي وَتَرۡحَمۡنِيٓ أَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ
11:47.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! in Thee do I seek refuge (from the sin) that I should ask of Thee that whereof I have no knowledge. Unless Thou forgive me and have mercy on me I shall be among the lost

49:14.ar: ۞قَالَتِ ٱلۡأَعۡرَابُ ءَامَنَّاۖ قُل لَّمۡ تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَلَٰكِن قُولُوٓاْ أَسۡلَمۡنَا وَلَمَّا يَدۡخُلِ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۖ وَإِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَا يَلِتۡكُم مِّنۡ أَعۡمَٰلِكُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
49:14.en: The wandering Arabs say: We believe. Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Ye believe not, but rather say "We submit," for the faith hath not yet entered into your hearts. Yet, if ye obey Allah and His messenger, He will not withhold from you aught of (the reward of) your deeds. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

91:9.en: He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow

91:10.en: And he is indeed a failure who stunteth it

18:103.en: Say: Shall We inform you who will be the greatest losers by their works

18:104.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعۡيُهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَهُمۡ يَحۡسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمۡ يُحۡسِنُونَ صُنۡعًا
18:104.en: Those whose effort goeth astray in the life of the world, and yet they reckon that they do good work

16:123.ar: ثُمَّ أَوۡحَيۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ أَنِ ٱتَّبِعۡ مِلَّةَ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفࣰ اۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
16:123.en: And afterward We inspired thee (Muhammad, saying): Follow the religion of Abraham, as one by nature upright. He was not of the idolaters

22:78.ar: وَجَٰهِدُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِۦۚ هُوَ ٱجۡتَبَىٰكُمۡ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲۚ مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَۚ هُوَ سَمَّىٰكُمُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ مِن قَبۡلُ وَفِي هَٰذَا لِيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِۚ فَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ هُوَ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ فَنِعۡمَ ٱلۡمَوۡلَىٰ وَنِعۡمَ ٱلنَّصِيرُ
22:78.en: And strive for Allah with the endeavour which is His right. He hath chosen you and hath not laid upon you in religion any hardship; the faith of your father Abraham (is yours). He hath named you Muslims of old time and in this (Scripture), that the messenger may be a witness against you, and that ye may be witnesses against mankind. So establish worship, pay the poor-due, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protecting friend. A blessed Patron and a blessed Helper

3:68.ar: إِنَّ أَوۡلَى ٱلنَّاسِ بِإِبۡرَٰهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ ٱتَّبَعُوهُ وَهَٰذَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
3:68.en: Lo! those of mankind who have the best claim to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet and those who believe (with him); and Allah is the Protecting Guardian of the believers

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

11:74.ar: فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنۡ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ ٱلرَّوۡعُ وَجَآءَتۡهُ ٱلۡبُشۡرَىٰ يُجَٰدِلُنَا فِي قَوۡمِ لُوطٍ
11:74.en: And when the awe departed from Abraham, and the glad news reached him, he pleaded with Us on behalf of the folk of Lot

11:75.en: Lo! Abraham was mild, imploring, penitent

11:76.ar: يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُ أَعۡرِضۡ عَنۡ هَٰذَآۖ إِنَّهُۥ قَدۡ جَآءَ أَمۡرُ رَبِّكَۖ وَإِنَّهُمۡ ءَاتِيهِمۡ عَذَابٌ غَيۡرُ مَرۡدُودࣲ‏
11:76.en: (It was said) O Abraham! Forsake this! Lo! thy Lord's commandment hath gone forth, and lo! there cometh unto them a doom which cannot be repelled

24:11.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلۡإِفۡكِ عُصۡبَةࣱ مِّنكُمۡۚ لَا تَحۡسَبُوهُ شَرࣰّ ا لَّكُمۖ بَلۡ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۚ لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُم مَّا ٱكۡتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِۚ وَٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبۡرَهُۥ مِنۡهُمۡ لَهُۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:11.en: Lo! they who spread the slander are a gang among you. Deem it not a bad thing for you; nay, it is good for you. Unto every man of them (will be paid) that which he hath earned of the sin; and as for him among them who had the greater share therein, his will be an awful doom

21:65.ar: ثُمَّ نُكِسُواْ عَلَىٰ رُءُوسِهِمۡ لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَ مَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ يَنطِقُونَ
21:65.en: And they were utterly confounded, and they said: Well thou knowest that these speak not

VqR8l8YvBQ0.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat al-Saffat 37:71-98 (Nuh and the Sound Heart of Ibrahim)
VqR8l8YvBQ0.one_line: Balancing reason and the unseen, then the stories of Nuh, whose son drowned and whose question was rebuked, and Ibrahim, who came to his Lord with a sound heart.
VqR8l8YvBQ0.summary: He insists on balance: Islam cannot be understood without reason, yet reason itself shows there is an unseen beyond it, and both extremes are wrong, the one who never thinks and the one who erases the unseen or drowns in superstition. Rational debate over rulings and evidence is good; delving into the unseen, people's intentions, who is saved, the evil eye or the mechanics of decree, harms people. Four verses sum up human history: most went astray, warners came, the warned were punished, except Allah's sincere servants. Each prophet in al-Saffat had something in his life whose wisdom was hidden. Nuh built a huge ship on a mountain far from water and was promised his family's rescue, yet his son drowned; Adnan admits this story troubled him for years. It teaches that parents cannot be judged for children who stray and that asking about the unseen is not our place, which is why Nuh will hesitate to intercede. He explains the four praises given to each prophet. Ibrahim is introduced with a sound heart, free of shirk and the heart's diseases; he was the great questioner who followed reason, and in this surah alone he is ordered to sacrifice his son, the test of obeying without seeing the wisdom.

outline.heading: Opening
The cluster and its angles on obedience
outline.gist: Al-Ahzab on obedience in hardship, Saba on societies, Fatir through knowledge, Ya-Sin through calling to Allah as the life of the soul.

outline.heading: Al-Saffat: obedience when the wisdom is hidden
outline.gist: Here the issue is not hardship but missing pieces; since Allah Himself is unseen, faith in Him is already faith in the unseen.

outline.heading: No call to switch off reason
outline.gist: Islam can only be understood, Allah only known and the law only derived through reason; there is simply an unseen beyond it, starting with the angels the surah swears by.

outline.heading: Everything after death is unseen
outline.gist: We memorized the blasts, scrolls, scales and bridge growing up Muslim, but all of it, the dialogues of the Day and the tree of Zaqqum included, is unseen and not ours to interrogate.

outline.heading: The seen is to the unseen as a womb to existence
outline.gist: Errors come from two directions: those who accept the unseen and never use reason, and those who reason but practically erase the unseen.

outline.heading: Reason itself shows there is an unseen
outline.gist: Blind following is the Quran's harshest blame; the mind can grasp that something may exist outside time and space, and emotions reduced to hormones still leave most of them unexplained.

outline.heading: Two bad approaches, one balance
outline.gist: Seeing only the sensory world ends in ruin, and seeing everything as unseen ends in superstition; the prophets' stories ahead show wisdom we cannot always see.

outline.heading: Most of the ancients went astray, except the sincere
outline.gist: Allah's wisdom in every ruling is real even if never reached; the sincere servant is again excepted from being held to his deeds.

outline.heading: Questions about the unseen versus rational debate
outline.gist: Why send warners again, why punish, why these few: these are unseen questions, unlike reasoned discussion of evidence and rulings, which he encourages.

outline.heading: Intentions are unseen too
outline.gist: Judging a scholar's or anyone's intention is delving into the unseen; the Prophet never allowed inferring intentions from actions, so we cannot rule on people's standing with Allah.

outline.heading: The ignorant love the unseen because there all are equal
outline.gist: Discussing knowledge takes study, while on the unseen the scholar knows no more than anyone; that is why people prefer arguing over who is saved.

outline.heading: The evil eye and decree: keep to the useful
outline.gist: Insisting something was certainly the eye is unseen; the useful part is ruqyah, seeking refuge and not flaunting blessings. Delving into the hidden side of decree led sects to fatalism and worse.

outline.heading: Four verses that sum up human history
outline.gist: Most went astray, warners came, the warned were punished, except the sincere; the rest of the details are hidden from us.

outline.heading: Reciting the story of Nuh
outline.gist: Nuh called, Allah answered, saved him and his family from the great distress, made his descendants the survivors and drowned the rest.

outline.heading: Why these prophets, and no story is repeated
outline.gist: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Harun, Ilyas, Lut and Yunus each appear for a reason tied to the surah's theme, and no story is told the same way twice.

outline.heading: Nuh's call and the best of responders
outline.gist: Nuh's story is brief here because each prophet in this surah faced something whose wisdom was hidden; his call was that his people disobeyed and he was overcome.

outline.heading: Saved with his family, but not his son
outline.gist: His wife was not counted as family, but he had been promised his family; distress is constriction joined with grief, and even Nuh, first of the resolute messengers, lost his son.

outline.heading: His descendants alone remained
outline.gist: Those who believed with him had no surviving offspring, so all humanity traces to his three sons; why that is so would change nothing in our conduct.

outline.heading: Did the flood cover the whole earth?
outline.gist: Reports of the People of the Book may be used carefully; there is no clear Quranic or hadith proof of a worldwide flood, and other punishments were local, so others may have lived on without descendants.

outline.heading: A ship on a mountain far from any water
outline.gist: Nuh built a huge ship for decades with no sea in sight while his people mocked; many lived and died without seeing the wisdom.

outline.heading: The son's death troubled him for years
outline.gist: He admits he wrestled with why Nuh's son drowned; it teaches us not to judge parents whose children go astray.

outline.heading: You cannot force your children's guidance
outline.gist: Nuh tried his utmost; parents are there to guide and support, not to compel, and if compulsion worked Nuh would have done it.

outline.heading: 'My son is of my family'
outline.gist: Nuh appealed to Allah's promise; Allah replied his son was not of his family, since disbelief cuts that bond, and told him not to ask about what he had no knowledge of.

outline.heading: Why Nuh will hesitate to intercede
outline.gist: A father's grief made him ask; he repented, and on the Day he will decline to intercede because he once asked about the unseen. Asking 'why did this happen to her son' is Shaytan's slope.

outline.heading: Peace upon Nuh among the worlds
outline.gist: Only Nuh gets 'among the worlds', because all humanity descends from him; 'we left for him' means lasting praise among later nations.

outline.heading: Four honours repeated for the prophets
outline.gist: Lasting good mention, peace from Allah meaning no punishment or reproach, being among the doers of good repaid in kind, and being among the believing servants.

outline.heading: Islam and iman: side by side or rising levels
outline.gist: Islam can mean practice and iman belief, or they can be ranks, Muslim, believer, then muhsin; being named a believer is high praise, as the Bedouins were told they had only submitted.

outline.heading: Reciting the start of Ibrahim's story
outline.gist: Ibrahim was of Nuh's party; he came with a sound heart, questioned his people's worship, looked at the stars and said he was unwell.

outline.heading: 'Of his party': following the same path
outline.gist: A shi'ah is a group that champions someone; Ibrahim came centuries after Nuh but carried the same teaching.

outline.heading: A story told only in al-Saffat
outline.gist: When a story appears in only one place, study that surah closely; part of Ibrahim's story appears nowhere else, coming in two or three weeks.

outline.heading: A sound heart
outline.gist: Free of shirk, vanity, pride, showing off, envy, hatred and heedlessness; the state of the heart decides whether deeds are accepted, and the worst shock is expecting success and failing.

outline.heading: Ibrahim, the Prophet's own model
outline.gist: Even the Prophet needed a model; he came to revive Ibrahim's way, met him in the seventh heaven, and hajj follows in Ibrahim's footsteps.

outline.heading: Everyone claims Ibrahim
outline.gist: No name is claimed by more people, but the closest to him are those who follow him; he was a man of reason, forever asking questions.

outline.heading: A young man in Iraq seeking only his Lord
outline.gist: Before twenty, among idol-worshippers, he argued only to reach the truth, without wanting fame, money or power; he had few followers in life and the most after death.

outline.heading: Reason and the unseen joined in one person
outline.gist: He asked how Allah revives the dead and argued with the angels over Lut's people; his story unites a questioning mind with faith in the unseen.

outline.heading: Inventing gods besides Allah
outline.gist: Ifk is a lie with no evidence at all; everyone agrees there is a creator, and modern atheism that denies causality is rejected by philosophers and logicians.

outline.heading: 'What do you think of the Lord of the worlds?'
outline.gist: A rebuke or a question; those who cannot answer by argument walk away. Looking at the stars is an Arab expression for deep thought.

outline.heading: 'I am unwell': one of Ibrahim's three statements
outline.gist: To stay behind from their festival he let them think the stars told him he was ill, meaning weariness of spirit; on the Day he fears this counted against him and sends people to Musa.

outline.heading: The idols, the fire and what is coming
outline.gist: He asks the idols why they do not eat or speak, strikes them, argues that Allah created them and what they carve, and is thrown into a great fire and comes out alive.

outline.heading: Where is the wisdom in sacrificing a son?
outline.gist: The man who followed logic in everything is given the greatest test: a command whose wisdom he cannot see. The story of the sacrifice appears only in al-Saffat.

aaaK1jz3YnU.title: Tafseer of Surat al-Hadid, Part 7: Verses 22-25
aaaK1jz3YnU.one_line: Why Allah tells us every calamity is pre-written, the pendulum of confidence and humility, self-centredness, and why the surah is named Iron.
aaaK1jz3YnU.summary: After urging listeners to learn and memorize the final quarter of the Quran a few verses at a time, he returns to verses 22 and 23. He clears away the old arguments about decree: a god who did not know the future would not deserve worship, knowing is not causing, time does not apply to Allah, and anyone sitting in the room can see they have real choices. The verse concerns what lies outside our control, like a never-smoking marathon runner's terminal cancer, and its stated purpose is practical: not to over-grieve losses with endless 'if onlys', nor to become entitled and vain over success that Allah often bailed us out to achieve. He describes an inner two-layer pendulum, confidence against vanity or worthlessness and humility against arrogance or inferiority, which life's bumps swing unless held in the middle by remembering that all was written. Vanity and arrogance produce self-centredness, which the verse calls stinginess, and a culture that encourages it; material events cause spiritual swings that return as material behaviour. Allah is the Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy, needing none of it. Verse 25 explains the surah's name: prophets were sent with the Book, the Balance and iron, so faith must be joined to strength and use of the world, a balance the Prophet embodied.

outline.heading: Opening
The comprehensive final quarter and its four clusters
outline.gist: The last four parts summarize all of Islam; the early Makkan cluster ending with al-Hadid differs in tone from the Madinan surahs that follow.

outline.heading: Learn a portion of the Quran with its meanings
outline.gist: Not everyone will memorize it all, but memorizing the few verses covered each week would by now give a full part one understands and can pray with.

outline.heading: The next cluster is full of stories
outline.gist: Unlike this cluster, the next part revolves around events in the companions' lives with revelation attached.

outline.heading: Recap: the cluster of decisions
outline.gist: Each surah forces a choice, except al-Hadid, which demands both appearance and essence.

outline.heading: The ummah's imbalance
outline.gist: Many Muslims are all mechanics, others claim spirituality without prayer; a community needs both values and wealth, strength and numbers.

outline.heading: No calamity on earth or in yourselves
outline.gist: No one questions Allah over good fortune; life always mixes good and bad, and the verse covers both outer events and inner afflictions.

outline.heading: Written in a record before He brought it to life
outline.gist: Kitab means a grouped record on one subject; all was documented before life appeared on earth, a vast step beyond mere matter.

outline.heading: Why tell us this at all?
outline.gist: Leave five men in a room long enough and they will argue about qadar; yet Allah had a specific benefit in mind.

outline.heading: A god who did not know would not deserve worship
outline.gist: Not knowing tomorrow is the essence of human fear and of life's adventure; Allah is not bound by that.

outline.heading: His knowledge is not like ours
outline.gist: We only know the future of something pre-programmed, like a toy car aimed at a wall; equating our knowledge with His is the root error.

outline.heading: You can see you have choices
outline.gist: Sects that denied free will ignore that we choose every moment; our options are limited by design but real.

outline.heading: Beyond time, and knowledge is not causal
outline.gist: We cannot imagine anything outside time and space; knowing chickens lay eggs does not make them lay, and the future is not future to Him.

outline.heading: The stated purpose: neither grieve nor exult
outline.gist: He told us so that we do not over-grieve what we lose or become vain over what we are given.

outline.heading: Decree versus what you brought on yourself
outline.gist: A falling piano, or an accident while driving carefully, is decree; an accident while speeding and texting is a consequence, and passing without studying is Allah giving the opposite of what you earned.

outline.heading: The marathon runner with lung cancer
outline.gist: His first patient conversation of that kind was a non-smoking 65-year-old runner who died within months: a hand dealt, written beforehand.

outline.heading: Do not drown in 'if only'
outline.gist: Grieve and hold yourself accountable, but accept what you did not cause and, for what you did, repent, learn and move on.

outline.heading: Success stories and entitlement
outline.gist: Tell the truth about how often Allah bailed you out; in the Quran farah means vain entitlement, not simple happiness.

outline.heading: Your package of good and bad
outline.gist: Everyone receives a different mix, none of it personal; be humble with good things and use them for others, and learn from bad ones.

outline.heading: Hardship as a source of empathy
outline.gist: Those who process calamities well become the best helpers, as former addicts make the best substance abuse counsellors.

outline.heading: List your blessings and your wounds
outline.gist: An exercise from his mentoring sessions: an honest inventory of strengths and harms, using the good to give back and preventing the bad for others.

outline.heading: The deepest fear: meaningless loss
outline.gist: Loss that no one sees or records is almost impossible to bear; knowing it was written gives it meaning and a story.

outline.heading: Material events cause spiritual swings
outline.gist: Despair and vanity are spiritual changes caused by material events, so the material and spiritual are linked whether or not one is religious.

outline.heading: Vanity and arrogance defined
outline.gist: Arrogance compares oneself to others; vanity is self-regard without comparison, believing oneself special and craving the spotlight.

outline.heading: The two-layer pendulum
outline.gist: Confidence can swing to vanity or worthlessness, humility to arrogance or inferiority; hold both in the middle through life's roller coaster.

outline.heading: Humbleness, and reading your own life
outline.gist: Confidence plus humility makes the humble person everyone loves; read your own experiences as an open book and learn from them.

outline.heading: Stinginess as self-centredness
outline.gist: Bukhl here is self-centredness, withholding emotion, empathy and love more than money; check that you are not such a person.

outline.heading: A culture that commands self-centredness
outline.gist: Modern life encourages exclusive focus on the self; self-centred spouses, friends and acquaintances drain those around them.

outline.heading: Event, swing, behaviour
outline.gist: A material event shifts the spirit, which produces material behaviour like refusing to lend without return; hence the surah's insistence on both.

outline.heading: Al-Ghani al-Hamid
outline.gist: Allah needs nothing and is always praiseworthy, while we deserve no vanity; that is why a Muslim answers 'alhamdulillah'.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recitation notes on heavy letters
outline.gist: Keep the seen light between heavy letters so it does not drift toward a sad.

outline.heading: Why the surah is called Iron
outline.gist: A surah so focused on the heart is named after the metal that revolutionized life, so no one separates spirituality from the material.

outline.heading: The Book and the Balance
outline.gist: Prophets came with clear proofs, revealed law and the mizan, a figurative balance, so people establish qist: justice with prosperity and mercy.

outline.heading: Iron: great might and benefits
outline.gist: Iron brings military strength and countless civilian benefits, and lets Allah show who supports Him and His messengers unseen.

outline.heading: Law and strength together
outline.gist: Prophets were sent with both guidance and power; the ummah began failing when it dropped one, and in truth has neglected both.

outline.heading: The Prophet's exquisite balance
outline.gist: Unparalleled spirituality joined with use of the material world, which is why within centuries Muslim scholars were also scientists.

14r5YRU0UCg.title: The Five Categories of Community Investment: Our Path Forward
14r5YRU0UCg.one_line: Closing the series: what the community needs, what holds it back, what strengths it already has, and a call to wake up.
14r5YRU0UCg.summary: Opening with the command to cooperate in righteousness and not in sin, he closes his series on five areas of community investment: education, mentorship, outreach, advocacy and financial centralization. Whether or not people accept his categories, he argues, a community without a plan will lose its identity and eventually its rights, as history repeatedly shows, and Muslims are obligated to pursue every form of strength. What is needed is leadership, not necessarily religious; organized teams that specialize instead of each doing everything; individual champions who take an idea forward rather than handing it to the imam; grit that outlasts the roughly eighteen-day wave of emotion; and sincere intention for Allah alone. The obstacles are passivity, negativity toward those who try, short attention spans, and above all division, which he illustrates with Andalus, where Muslim rulers allied with enemies against each other and were destroyed. Muslims need not like one another to stand together. He also asks where the tens of thousands of Muslims in the city who never attend Jumuah are. In the second khutbah he lists strengths: professionals, cooperative institutions, a youthful community like the Prophet's first followers, people in key positions, and wealth. Recalling how he had a dictatorship to blame in Syria, he says there is no excuse here and urges the community to wake up.

outline.heading: Opening
Cooperate in righteousness: we need a plan
outline.gist: With the verse on cooperating in righteousness and not in sin, he closes the series: agree with his categories or not, without a plan whoever stands here in ten or thirty years will describe the same struggles, or worse.

outline.heading: Those who do not defend small rights lose them all
outline.gist: This is the story of the world: groups that do not work toward common goals lose their identity, and those who let even a little of their rights go eventually lose all of them.

outline.heading: Our deficit is history
outline.gist: Charters and treaties have always existed and change nothing. The ummah does not know history, its own least of all, and must learn from those before it to avoid repeating it.

outline.heading: Obligated to seek every form of strength
outline.gist: Allah obligates the community to build social, academic, intellectual, financial and political strength. A community's strength adds up from what its individuals achieve, so it must know its strengths and deficits.

outline.heading: These five are within our strength
outline.gist: He chose the categories because the community has the ability to act on them and runs deficits in each, and communities that focused on versions of them achieved a great deal.

outline.heading: Need: leadership, not necessarily religious
outline.gist: No category moves forward without some leadership to channel the community's energy, and he does not think religious leadership is the kind required.

outline.heading: Need: organized, specialized teamwork
outline.gist: Instead of everyone opening a shop to do everything, groups and institutions should each take a category they have the skills and resources for; trying to do everything ends in doing nothing.

outline.heading: Need: champions who carry their own ideas
outline.gist: The community's most abundant resource is ideas, which people drop off with the imam and walk away from. Whoever has a worthwhile idea should champion it, find like-minded people and build it for the sake of Allah.

outline.heading: Need: grit that outlasts the eighteen-day wave
outline.gist: Emotion comes in waves: by his count the community talks about any crisis for seventeen or eighteen days, gets bored and moves on while the problem stays. Work must continue until it is solved.

outline.heading: Need: sincere intention for Allah alone
outline.gist: Not just good or strong intentions but sincere ones, with no fame, wealth, status or agenda behind them; fixing the intention when volunteering is the hardest part.

outline.heading: Obstacle: passivity
outline.gist: People complain but never step into an initiative, and when one exists the talk is only about its flaws, though every human effort is flawed.

outline.heading: Obstacle: negativity
outline.gist: Either get in line and help or at least do not be negative. The community is very critical with very little output; those who criticize everything often do nothing, a problem of the nafs.

outline.heading: Obstacle: interest that fades in two weeks
outline.gist: Some country will bomb another, everyone will speak for two weeks and then forget. He then turns to the obstacle he most wants to address: division, which everyone knows conquers.

outline.heading: Division at a disadvantage
outline.gist: The community is small, marginalized and carries a bad reputation from long propaganda; adding internal division to that is a serious problem. He urges everyone to read the history of Andalus.

outline.heading: The fall of Andalus
outline.gist: Muslim rulers took as allies those who clearly wanted to destroy them in order to defeat other Muslims, then were slaughtered by those same allies. The pattern recurs today as ideological tyranny, intellectual oppression and systemic marginalization.

outline.heading: You do not have to like each other
outline.gist: Liking one another is irrelevant; you can disagree fundamentally and he is still your brother, and each owes the other support.

outline.heading: Do not divide like those before you
outline.gist: The Quran is full of the warning not to do what earlier communities did: they divided and ruined everything.

outline.heading: Division costs the next generation's identity
outline.gist: A minority cannot afford silos working in isolation. The masajid will stay open; the loss will be the next generation's identity in an ideological conflict over values and what may be said and taught.

outline.heading: Where are the Muslims who never come?
outline.gist: Perhaps four thousand attend Jumuah across the city while far more Muslims live here. Who are they, what keeps them away and what do they need? Without answers there is no way forward.

outline.heading: Interlude
Strength: accomplished professionals
outline.gist: The number of highly skilled entrepreneurs and professionals with degrees and accomplishments is astonishing, yet there is little fruit to show for it.

outline.heading: Strength: institutions that are not at war
outline.gist: The city's Islamic institutions know each other, have collaborated and can do more, with none of the open public animosity seen elsewhere in North America.

outline.heading: Strength: a youthful community
outline.gist: Its greatest asset is its many motivated young people of both genders, who can go far if given leadership, opportunity, mentorship, training and support.

outline.heading: Young like the first Muslims; already in key positions
outline.gist: The Prophet built Islam on the young: the median age of the first few hundred Muslims was about 26. Muslims also already hold important positions across the city and country.

outline.heading: Wealth and numbers, yet nothing gets done
outline.gist: With wealth, numbers and assets, he has no answer for why the community cannot give its young the tools to be strong Muslims with their identity, language, book and narrative.

outline.heading: Reporting his Quran students to Syrian intelligence
outline.gist: From seventeen, every month for six years, he had to write down the names of the young children he taught Quran in a room with a chair, a table and a tire hung from the ceiling.

outline.heading: No one to blame here
